## (1) First message to the user

Here are the premises before we start. I could not open primary code in this pass, so each source below is the gather draft. I name the lookup each one still needs.

- **Supported:** The reports page renders a table and has no export action today. Source: the gather draft's recon of the reports page.
- **Supported:** `src/export/csv.ts` already builds CSV from the table's column definitions. This means the "every column shown in the table" row can reuse the column list instead of keeping a second one. Source: the draft's `Pattern:` line. I still need to read that file to confirm its signature.
- **Corrected:** The ticket's 10k-row/60s row assumes the report data can be fetched in bounded chunks. The draft records that paging is unimplemented, so this is a missing implicit dependency. Lookup: the draft's recon of the report data path. Result: no paging exists. The design will have to add it or show it is not needed.
- **Unverified:** Whether an export of 10k rows finishes under 60s with today's single fetch. The draft names no measurement and no benchmark. Nothing suggests the target is impossible. This goes into Open Questions, and the row stays `in-scope`.

On scope: the ticket groups its rows by repo, and this repo is `acme/widgets` (overrides `## Issue tracker`).

- The three `acme/widgets` rows are `in-scope`.
- "Exports are emailed to the requesting user" sits under `acme/mailer`, so it is `elsewhere: acme/mailer`.

The framing holds: I checked the reports page's missing export action, the column-definition reuse in `src/export/csv.ts`, and the report data path (no paging). I also checked the scout's note that the 60s row is hard. That note offered no alternative and no evidence the row is wrong, so it is not a framing concern.

Where should the Export CSV button appear on the reports page?
A) Beside the report title
B) In the table's toolbar, above the column headers
C) In a page-level actions menu
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - a title-adjacent action is visible without scrolling and needs no new menu surface.

---

## (2) Approaches message

First, a restatement of the missing dependency. Paging for the report data is not implemented. The lookup was the gather draft's recon of the report data path, which found no paging. The 10k-row/60s row depends on fetching the report in bounded chunks. Whether a single unpaged fetch meets 60s is unverified, because no measurement exists.

So far: the button goes beside the report title, and the export uses the visible table columns in table order.

The approaches differ on how the export gets 10k rows of data to the serializer.

**Recommended: reuse the CSV serializer and add paging to the report data fetch.**
- How it works: the button handler pulls the report one page at a time. It feeds each page's rows to `src/export/csv.ts`, using the table's visible column definitions in table order. Then it assembles the file for download.
- Why: this is the only option that bounds each fetch, and the 10k/60s row is in-scope with no evidence that one fetch fits the budget.
- Trade-off: paging is a new capability on the report data path. Any other reader of that path sees the added page parameters, so the design must keep them optional.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button beside the report title; paging parameters on the report data fetch; a page loop in the export handler; tests for column order/visibility and for a 10k-row export under 60s
Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts`'s use of the table's column definitions; extends the existing report data fetch rather than adding a parallel data path.

**Reuse-only: the CSV serializer with a single unpaged fetch.**
- How it works: the button handler fetches the whole report in one request and passes it to `src/export/csv.ts`. Nothing new is built besides the button.
- Trade-off: it is the smallest change. Its gap is the 60s row: a single fetch of 10k rows is the unmeasured case, and nothing bounds it if the report grows.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button beside the report title; a call from it into `src/export/csv.ts` with the visible columns; tests for column order/visibility and the 10k-row timing
Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts`'s use of the table's column definitions; no new construct.

**Drop the "export is a synchronous download" assumption: run the export as a server-side background job.**
- How it works: the button enqueues a job that serializes the report and offers the file for download when it is ready.
- Trade-off: this removes the 60s pressure from the request. But it adds a job runner and a ready-file handoff. It also overlaps with the `acme/mailer` delivery row, which belongs to another repo.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button; an export job type; job status/download endpoint; a ready-file notification in the UI; job and download tests
Pattern: cuts across the current pattern - the gather cites no job runner, so this adds a new boundary beside `src/export/csv.ts` for one feature.

**What would flip the recommendation:** if a measured unpaged export of a 10k-row report finishes well under 60s on representative data, reuse-only meets every in-scope row with no new construct and becomes the recommendation.

Which approach should the design use?
A) Reuse the serializer and add paging
B) Reuse-only, single fetch
C) Background export job
Recommendation: A - it is the only option that bounds each fetch for the in-scope 10k/60s row without adding a new job boundary.

## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds against the supplied observations: the reports page lacks an export action, and the draft identifies the table’s column definitions and `src/export/csv.ts` as the reuse path. I cannot independently verify the callers, column-selection data flow, or serializer behavior without primary code; those remain assumptions to check, not established findings.

Paging is missing according to the draft. That is an implementation dependency—not evidence that the 10k-row, under-60-second requirement is impossible. All three `acme/widgets` acceptance criteria remain **in-scope**, including that performance requirement. The email criterion belongs to `acme/mailer` and receives `elsewhere: acme/mailer`; this work does not add email delivery.

I’ll carry your recorded decisions forward: place **Export CSV beside the report title**, export **the visible table columns in table order**, and **reuse the existing CSV serializer with added paging**. The Design will explicitly record the visible-column interpretation while preserving the ticket’s acceptance-criteria text verbatim.

## 2. Approaches message

**I recommend reusing the existing CSV serializer and adding paging**, as you selected.

Before comparing approaches, the unresolved dependencies are explicit: the gather draft says paging is unimplemented, but no primary implementation is available here to establish its owning API or retrieval contract. It names `src/export/csv.ts` and the table’s column definitions, but their callers, handling of visible-column order, and support for paged input cannot be independently checked. No measured 10k-row export result is supplied, so compliance with the 60-second requirement remains unverified—not disproved.

The main distinction is **extending the existing export path versus introducing a separate export boundary**.

### A) Extend the existing serializer and add paging — recommended

Pass the visible table-column sequence into the existing CSV path and retrieve the report’s rows through paging. Keep column selection and ordering tied to the table’s definitions rather than maintaining a second export schema.

This is the minimal reuse-only candidate: adding parameters or branches to an existing construct does not require a separate export subsystem. Its blast radius includes any existing serializer callers, whose behavior must remain compatible. The design must also establish that paging covers the report without missing or duplicating rows and that the complete export meets the ticket’s performance requirement.

Removes: none.  
Adds: the reports-page button beside the title; its export handler; visible-column/order input to the existing serializer where needed; paged row retrieval; correctness and performance coverage.  
Pattern: Follows the shared-column reuse path identified in `src/export/csv.ts` by the gather draft; caller compatibility and the actual signatures remain to be verified.

### B) Add a dedicated export execution boundary

Keep the same button and visible-column contract, but move report retrieval and CSV production behind a dedicated export operation, reusing the existing serializer where compatible.

This drops the assumption that the table’s own loading path must also execute the complete export. It could provide better isolation if that path cannot efficiently retrieve a whole report. However, it adds a contract and execution boundary whose necessity is not established by the supplied observations; it must not introduce a parallel column schema.

Removes: none.  
Adds: the reports-page button and handler; a dedicated export operation and its request/result contract; paged retrieval within that operation; integration with the existing serializer; correctness and performance coverage.  
Pattern: Preserves the shared-column principle identified at `src/export/csv.ts`, but introduces a new boundary rather than extending the existing path; repository precedent for that boundary is unverified.

Your recorded choice is **A**. I would revisit it only if inspection or measurement shows that the existing path cannot satisfy the approved full-report export and performance requirements—not merely because paging needs implementation.
